subject: biology
title: Reaction Times & Neurones
welcome_lead: Today you'll measure how fast your nerves fire and see why synapses slow things down.
meta_desc: GCSE Biology reaction time required practical — ruler drop, neurone types, synaptic delay.
final_note: You learned the ruler drop method, the three neurone types, and why synapses add tiny delays.

concepts.def: Time between a stimulus and your response
Carries signals from receptors to the CNS
Connects sensory and motor neurones in the CNS
Carries signals from the CNS to an effector
Chemical that carries a signal across a synapse
Measures reaction time using how far a ruler falls

walkthroughs.body_html:
A partner holds a ruler at the 0 cm mark above your open hand.

They drop it without warning and you catch it. Read the cm mark at your thumb.

Use t = √(2d/g) where d is in metres and g = 9.8 m/s². Repeat and average to make it reliable.

Three jobs, three neurones.

Sensory = receptor to CNS. Relay = inside the CNS, links the others. Motor = CNS to effector.

In a reflex arc the signal hops sensory → relay → motor.

Electrical signals fly along a neurone fast.

But at a synapse the signal becomes a chemical — neurotransmitter molecules must diffuse across the gap.

That tiny diffusion step adds delay. More synapses = slower overall response.
